source_name: Atamya (www.atamya.com - Agentic PIM with an embedded bpmn.io / Flowable BPMN engine)
enumeration_method: robots.txt -> sitemap_index.xml -> 9 Yoast sub-sitemaps (post 178, page 111, jobs 3, event-aufzeichnungen 21, downloads 32, events 6, marketplace 27, glossar 102, author 16); deduplicated across the en/de hreflang variants to 496 unique URLs (267 /de/ + 229 /en/). No keyword facet was used: the sitemap is the site's own complete enumeration and every one of the 496 URLs was fetched by direct HTTP at ~1 req/s with 0 failures. Pages are judged on the fetched body plus every content image (wp-content/uploads images inside the content modules, i.e. after removing the header/mega-menu and the footer, and after excluding the 11 images that recur on 25+ pages as theme chrome); all 439 distinct content images were downloaded and viewed as thumbnail contact sheets, the diagram-shaped ones at 258 px and the finalists at native resolution. The image census was taken from the static HTML of each fetched body: the theme lazy-loads every figure through data-lazy-src / data-lazy-sizes and srcset, and a raw-HTML audit found no figure that only JavaScript inserts, so no page had to be executed to enumerate its images. The v4 feature inventory holds 822 content-image entries (404 distinct files) plus 1497 page-image entries (642 distinct files); 29 image URLs referenced by the HTML are no longer retrievable (17 theme icons serving .svg, plus 12 uploads - whitepaper/download covers and three product teasers, mostly German teasers the vendor has since renamed). Those are chrome, not content, so no judgement rests on them and none of the 496 pages was blocked.
note: Vendor claim, verified on the pages themselves: ATAMYA is a German PIM whose workflow engine is BPMN 2.0 - 'By implementing "bpmn.io" and Flowable Expression Language, ATAMYA utilizes established open-source standards' (ai-powered-workflows), 'Workflow management pursuant to BPMN version 2.0' (user-and-workflow-management) - and whose central AI claim is a placement claim: 'Every AI call in ATAMYA is a native BPMN service task' (ai-foundations), 'AI is a native service task - integrated, orchestrated, and governed by the BPMN engine' (the figure caption on the ai-powered-workflows hero diagram). Two judgement conventions were applied and are the standing questions of this source. Q1 (notation): ATAMYA publishes two rendering styles - the real bpmn.io canvas (a live-editor screenshot, with gear-marked service tasks, person-marked user tasks, X/+ gateway diamonds) and a stylised marketing render that keeps the BPMN element semantics (start/end circles, gateway diamonds carrying the X and + markers, sequence-flow arrows, tasks carrying the element-type icons) but draws the tasks as squares and drops the labels into a legend underneath. The stylised render is judged UNCERTAIN with Q1 attached rather than E1, because the element semantics are BPMN's. Q2 (AI element): several of the real BPMN models carry service tasks whose AI binding is not marked in the diagram ('Generate Text', 'Start DeepL Translation', 'Automatic Categorization'), while the same site classifies text generation and DeepL translation as AI work ('Use AI Tools like DeepL', 'Translate Content', the AI-tasks figure) and the AI Foundations page asserts that 'Every AI call in ATAMYA is a native BPMN service task'. Those rows are UNCERTAIN with Q2 attached, never E2, per the E2 rule that an element whose implementation might be AI-bound but is not visible must not be excluded. Atamya publishes most pages as a DE/EN pair; where the same diagram file is served on both language URLs the second page is an E3 duplicate naming the first, and where a translated re-render exists instead the second page is UNCERTAIN with the duplicate question attached, since E3 is sanctioned only for the same diagram. Final pass (the figure group): the 104 pages whose content images contain a non-chrome figure were judged on the images themselves - contact sheets over every distinct image of the group, then native-resolution zooms of each candidate - not on the page copy alone. Boundary rule used: E0 when a figure carries no process at any level (hero graphic, statistic chart, comparison overview, photograph, UI screenshot); E1 only when a figure is process-shaped and demonstrably not BPMN - no events, no gateways, no pools, no sequence flows (step and icon chains, pipelines, cycle diagrams, panel illustrations); a figure that keeps BPMN element semantics but not the notation is UNCERTAIN with Q1, never E1. E3 is written only where the twin page of a byte-identical file already carries a record (4 rows); where the shared figure was itself excluded, the second page receives the same E0/E1 code with a note naming the twin page, so that no exclusion is laundered into a duplicate claim. The figure group resolved to 9 INCLUDE, 3 UNCERTAIN (the standing Q1/Q2 questions), 14 E1, 2 E2 (plain BPMN whose page's only AI mention is a related-article teaser), 4 E3 and 72 E0; with the 392 non-figure pages that is 496 rows in total.
